questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Courses within my area of interest and interesting surroundings to explore during spare time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I don't recall exactly, but I remember it as being fairly easy to get the different information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't recall.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: One dorm.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Fully equipped kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a nice place, you don't need to bring much yourself. Different social events but also possible to be on your own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't recall the exact process, but first I applied to Tromsø and then to my courses at UNIS through Tromsø. A bit confusing and you get the final acceptance very late in comparison to other places, so it is hard to apply for different grants, and also hard to find a plan B in case you don't get in at UNIS.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always write my supervisor at UiT and UCPH.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get in at first, since it was not clear rom my transcript of records, that I had the sufficient ECTS in math. But other than that, it was succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make a plan B before applying for UNIS, so that you know what to do in case you don't get in. Apply through a university, where you find the courses interesting, so that you can go there instead.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Higher level than I was used to, but also possible to get a lot of help and guidance.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We had classes every day and very little time off to study on our own in comparison to UCPH. Otherwise very similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Polar Ocean Climate (AGF-214) and Polar Meteorology and Climate (AGF-213)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the courses that I did (Polar Ocean Climate (AGF-214) and Polar Meteorology and Climate (AGF-213), since they were very interesting, if you are into Arctic climate. As a Geographer these two courses were also a bit out of our area of expertise (a lot of math and derivation of equations), so it was very challenging. If possible, do the Physical Geography courses instead, if they are not cancelled again.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some food is very expensive on Svalbard, but it is possible to spend little money if you look for the right stuff. Also it was a bit more expensive in total for the rifle license and renting rifles/flare guns on the weekends.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sports with Svalbard Turn and hiking/cabin trips with the student group. Some different social events with Samskipnaden.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking while there is still sunlight and hunting for northern lights when it is dark.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the cabin while it is still light outside, it is very beautiful and nice to do some other hikes than the ones around Longyearbyen

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, since Norwegian and Danish are very similar in both language and culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go with the hiking group, it is a nice way to meet new people while being active.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No big cultural differences, really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fact that the local community seems very welcoming to newcomers. And that everyone who lives there loves the place and wants to protect it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The darkness is really tough, more than you realize, so remember to share that with your fellow students. The classes can also be difficult, but the most important thing is to ask whenever you have any questions. Since everyone at UNIS have different backgrounds there's no shame in asking. And lastly, the pool is relatively warm and there is a nice sauna, so go enjoy some heat there every once in a while :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I succeeded and passed some challenging courses, and that I learned a great deal about myself being in the field with the other students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The loneliness and darkness.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Svalbard is an amazing experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
